changes.after: A data frame is a table with rows and named columns.

before: data.frame(topic=c("a","b"), score=c(2,4)) combines two columns. Columns may have different types while each describes the same number of rows.
frame[1, "score"] selects row 1 from the score column. An empty row position means all rows; row and column positions are not interchangeable.

frame$score extracts that column. A row normally combines observations across several columns, rather than being a single variable.

For this data frame, $ receives the fixed column name score and returns its numeric column vector, not one selected row.
```r
frame <- data.frame(topic = c("a", "b"), score = c(2, 4))
cat(frame$score, sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
2,4
```
